newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open flat to 2.00 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open flat to 2.00 lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open unchanged to 2.00 cents per lb lower on Thursday, after the London market failed to make its $70 higher due, traders said.
London robusta futures came in some $29 higher on Thursday, but dealings were thin amid a lack of fresh fundamentals. At the midday break, benchmark LIFFE September was up $25, to $1,875.

Wednesday, New York arabica futures ended higher, lifted by an afternoon bout of trade and local buying. September rose 5.05 cents per lb, to 180.15, after ranging from 181.00 to 174.50. Spot July finished 2.00 cents higher, at 200.00, while the outer months closed up 0.50 to 3.05.
The July/September switch narrowed to 19.85 cents, from 22.90 cents at the close on Tuesday, while September/December widened to 22.75 cents compared with 20.75 cents.

On the charts, traders said the September contract would face near-term support at 174.00, with major support seen at 168.75 cents, a low reached last week. Resistance was pegged at 185.00 cents, followed by 192.00-194.00 cents.
Traders said, however, dwindling exchange-certified coffee stocks would continued to underpin the market.
After Wednesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 248 60-kg bags as of June 24, to 45,927 bags. There were 10,387 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
On the weather front, no damaging cold is expected in the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Thursday.
